appraisal_events.evidence: "M. de Norpois leur aurait dit ... que vous étiez un flatteur à moitié hystérique" — said at a dinner at the princesse de Guermantes's, and reported back to him by Mme Swann.
appraisal_events.explanation: Behind his back, Norpois has fixed a contemptuous verdict on the narrator which has travelled into the Guermantes circle where he believed himself unknown; the narration neither dismisses the judgment nor accepts it, comparing such outside images to an X-ray that may be unflattering yet true.

appraisal_events.evidence: To the narrator's remark that Saint-Loup calls Norpois "une peste", Mme Swann answers "— Il a raison"; and of his slander, "on savait trop de quelle bouche cela tombait".
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Swann ratifies Saint-Loup's verdict on Norpois and reports that his company discounted his words on account of their source, so the ambassador is locally convicted of malice.

status_effects.explanation: An insulting image of him has circulated at a Guermantes dinner table where he thought himself invisible, though the same report notes that no one there attached importance to it.
Norpois is confirmed as a treacherous talker whose word is discounted, undercutting the narrator's opening remark that he is 'sympathique'.

ambiguities: Norpois's verdict on the narrator is relayed at second hand and explicitly minimized by Mme Swann, while the narrator's meditation on the X-ray image of oneself grants such alien portraits a possible unflattering truth; the passage leaves the endorsement of the insult genuinely open.
